fields.reasoning: Each rebased head waits 2-7 minutes for CI, and on a main where several plan runs merge render PRs, another merge often lands in that window. Raising the cap to ship-change's keeps the two workflows' merge loops alike and follows the earlier Decision's rule; serialising merges would be a new mechanism outside this bug's scope.
fields.statement: The plan and plan-milestone workflows cap their merge loop's steps (rebase, wait-rebased, rebased-green and merge) at 6 visits each, ship-change's current cap for the same loop, so a plan PR on a busy main gets six rebase-and-merge tries before the run ends failed; the other steps' caps are unchanged
fields.wording: (derived) plan-merge-loops-to-rebase gave the plan workflows ship-change's cap; ship-change's merge loop is now 6 visits and the plan workflows kept 3, which run 01M7AH6RHKMZRAHGJKJFM4VTNT exhausted on a busy main

set.acceptance: TestPlanRerunsCIFlakes in internal/workflow/workflow_test.go checks, for both the built-in plan and plan-milestone workflows, that merge routes fail to rebase and that rebase, wait-rebased, rebased-green and merge each have max_visits 6 (wait-pr 3 and pr-green 4 unchanged), and fails if any is 3; cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/plan-workflow-merge-main-moved.txtar still passes as written; a new testscript cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/plan-workflow-merge-main-moved-often.txtar, modelled on it, has the fake gh push a commit to origin's main after each of the first three rebased-green checks: the run's log shows merge (visits 1, 2 and 3) fail then rebase, merge (visit 4) pass then close-out, gh.log has exactly one pr merge call, pinned to the fourth rebased head, no 'went over max_visits' appears, and the run ends succeeded. Files: internal/workflow/builtin/plan.toml, internal/workflow/builtin/plan-milestone.toml (the steps and the 'up to 3 times' comments), internal/workflow/workflow_test.go, cmd/rhiza/testdata/script/plan-workflow-merge-main-moved-often.txtar
set.statement: When a plan or plan-milestone run's merge finds origin/main has moved past the PR's checked head, the run goes back to rebase onto the new main (settling rendered-only conflicts by rendering again), waits for the rebased head's CI and merges it, up to 6 times (rebase, wait-rebased, rebased-green and merge each max_visits 6, ship-change's cap), instead of ending the run with 'Not merged'
